summary: SSO cookie rotation invalidates active CLI sessions during admin impersonation
description: Several internal engineers reported being abruptly logged out of the Redwood Console and CLI while performing admin impersonation (sudo-style flow) after a staged Okta configuration change was rolled. The issue manifested as immediate 401s from the auth-proxy and failed token exchanges for active CLI sessions; browser sessions were intermittently preserved for the same users. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and postmortem actions.
impact: Approximately 12 active developer/admin sessions across multiple teams were invalidated over a 3-hour window. CI jobs that relied on long-lived CLI tokens failed (3 pipelines). Internal support pages and a couple of emergency access requests were opened. No customer-facing traffic was affected, but internal deployment cadence was disrupted during the incident window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to Console via Okta SSO (device-trust enabled) and start an admin impersonation session (sudo -> assume-role via console 'Act as' feature).
2) Open a long-running terminal that authenticates via redwood-cli using the same Okta-backed session (token exchange + short TTL refresh enabled).
3) Trigger an Okta session cookie rotation (internal change rolled via feature flag); observe CLI token exchange attempts after rotation.

4) Expected: CLI should transparently refresh or reauthorize without breaking active shell. Observed: immediate 401 from auth-proxy and CLI prompts for re-login; console session sometimes persisted depending on browser cookie timing.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:03:12Z auth-proxy ERROR token-exchange: refresh failed: invalid_grant (okta-session-rotated)
2026-03-12T15:03:13Z cli-proxy WARN session: user=jenna.s incoming-cookie-fingerprint mismatch (prev=0x8a3b, now=0xc1f9)
2026-03-12T15:04:02Z console INFO impersonation-start: user=devops-admin target=bob.k session_id=svc-imp-7741
investigation: 2026-03-12 15:10 - Triage: Support confirmed multiple independent reports and elevated to SRE/Identity team.

Hypothesis A: Okta session rotation feature (cookie fingerprint rotation) invalidates internal session fingerprint used by auth-proxy, causing immediate token-exchange failures for CLI flows that depend on prior handshake.
Hypothesis B: Admin impersonation flow attaches additional short-lived claims that are not re-bound after Okta re-issuance, leading to RBAC lookup failure during token refresh.

Observed: Browser console sessions often persisted because front-end uses silent SSO with prompt=none and obtains new id_token; redwood-cli does a server-side token exchange and relies on a fingerprint that was rotated, producing invalid_grant.
Telemetry: Spike in 401s from auth-proxy at 15:02-15:10 UTC correlated with Okta tenant feature flag rollout. Affected users had CLI tokens minted within 30 minutes prior to rotation.
Reproduction validated in staging by toggling Okta rotation flag and initiating admin-impersonation CLI flow; reproduced reliably.
resolution: Immediate mitigation (15:30 UTC): Rolled back Okta cookie-rotation feature flag for the affected tenant to stop further invalidations.

Hotfix (16:20 UTC): Deployed auth-proxy change to tolerate one fingerprint rotation window during token-exchange (accept previous fingerprint for 5 minutes while attempting background rebind). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/2742

CLI patch (17:50 UTC): Release redwood-cli v0.12.7 with improved retry: on 401 with reason 'invalid_grant' attempt in-band interactive reauth or fallback to web-based SSO flow before failing hard. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/809
Validation: After rollout, no new token-exchange failures observed in 24-hour monitoring window and CI pipelines recovered once developers reauthenticated.
